about: Task 1426 — marker conservation across a suggestion splice. Both markerConservationViolation (src/lib/marker-conservation.ts) and marker_conservation_violation (editor/scripts/_common.py) must answer every case exactly as `expected` records. Readers: src/lib/__tests__/marker-conservation-parity.test.ts and editor/scripts/tests/test_marker_conservation.py.

cases.name: rewrite-carries-citation
cases.why: The doctrine case: an AI rewrite of a cited sentence carries its \vcid through verbatim — this was refused as stale before task 1426.

cases.name: plain-rewrite-no-markers
cases.why: A span with no markers rewritten with none — the overwhelmingly common case stays free.

cases.name: rewrite-drops-citation
cases.why: A rewrite that loses the \vcid would detach citation card c1 from its atom (a fresh id is minted on the next parse).

cases.name: rewrite-drops-footnote
cases.why: A rewrite whose span holds \vfid{f002}\footnote{…} and omits it would delete the user's footnote prose from the .tex.
cases.matched: polemical asides\vfid{f002}\footnote{The standard study.}. The gloss

cases.name: rewrite-introduces-new-id
cases.why: A marker the match never held mints an atom no card owns — task 035's phantom, still refused.

cases.name: rewrite-duplicates-an-id
cases.why: Re-landing an id MORE often than the match held it would make two atoms claim one card.

cases.name: rewrite-splits-range-pair
cases.why: A span straddling another card's range whose replacement keeps \vlid but loses \vlidend leaves an unpaired marker.

cases.name: rewrite-carries-range-pair
cases.why: A range wholly inside the span, carried through, keeps its card's anchor.

cases.name: vlidend-is-not-vlid
cases.why: Longest-first: \vlidend{x} must never be read as \vlid, or a swap would pass.

cases.name: introduced-reported-before-dropped
cases.why: Pins the report order: introduced (replacement order) before dropped (match order).

cases.name: cut-takes-citation
cases.why: A whole cut may take a citation with it when the atom is inside the cut.

cases.name: cut-takes-whole-range
cases.why: Another card's range lying wholly inside the cut simply goes with it.

cases.name: cut-splits-range
cases.why: A cut that removes only the start of a range leaves its \vlidend unpaired in the paragraph.

cases.name: cut-refuses-footnote
cases.why: Cutting a \vfid deletes the footnote's prose and orphans its card — a cut may not remove a footnote.

cases.name: cut-leaves-atom-behind
cases.why: A cut ending right after \vcid strips the id but leaves the \citet — the card detaches.

cases.name: cutter-rewrite-is-strict
cases.why: A Cutter suggestion WITH a replacement is a rewrite, not a whole cut — it conserves exactly.

cases.name: human-text-may-leave-out-a-citation
cases.why: A person's own replacement (user_text) is typed where markers are invisible; leaving a citation out is their edit, not a dropped marker.

cases.name: human-text-still-may-not-mint
cases.why: A marker a person did type must still not mint a phantom atom no card owns.

cases.name: rewrite-keeps-footnote-marker-drops-footnote
cases.why: Task 1484: keeping \vfid{f002} but deleting its \footnote{…} deletes the footnote prose and orphans the card — the marker multiset alone is conserved, so this passed before.
cases.matched: asides\vfid{f002}\footnote{The standard study \emph{is} here.}. The gloss

cases.name: rewrite-moves-footnote-away-from-marker
cases.why: An id binds the IMMEDIATELY following atom; a footnote moved away from its \vfid is a fresh footnote, and the card's marker binds nothing.
cases.matched: asides\vfid{f002}\footnote{The standard study \emph{is} here.}. The gloss

cases.name: rewrite-edits-footnote-body
cases.why: An AI rewrite of the paragraph may not silently rewrite the footnote's own prose; that is the footnote's card's business.
cases.matched: asides\vfid{f002}\footnote{The standard study \emph{is} here.}. The gloss

cases.name: rewrite-moves-marker-and-footnote-together
cases.why: A rewrite may MOVE the (marker, footnote) pair as a unit — only splitting it is refused.
cases.matched: asides\vfid{f002}\footnote{The standard study \emph{is} here.}. The gloss
cases.replacement: The gloss, with asides\vfid{f002}\footnote{The standard study \emph{is} here.}.

cases.name: rewrite-keeps-citation-marker-changes-key
cases.why: The \vcid's \citet{foo} is its atom; swapping the key under a kept id points citation card c1 at another work.

cases.name: span-ending-at-marker-must-still-end-there
cases.why: When the atom lies past the span, the replacement must end right at the marker too — anything after it would sit between the id and its atom.

cases.name: span-ending-at-marker-carried-verbatim
cases.why: The atom past the span is untouched when the replacement ends at the marker as the span did.

cases.name: cut-takes-citation-command-without-argument
cases.why: Task 1484: a cut over `\vcid{c1}\citet` but not its {…} strands `{foo}` in the text — the cut must cover the WHOLE atom.

cases.name: cut-takes-citation-with-optional-args
cases.why: A whole cut over a citation with optional args and its balanced key takes the atom with it.

cases.name: multicite-rewrite-drops-second-unit
cases.why: Task 1560: a plural \cites takes its [pre][post]{key} unit REPEATED — the atom ends after the LAST unit, so a rewrite keeping only the first silently drops key b from the citation.
cases.replacement: This is shown by \vcid{c1}\cites[p. 1]{a} shows this.

cases.name: multicite-rewrite-carries-every-unit
cases.why: Task 1560: the same plural citation carried through with all its units is a conserving rewrite.

cases.name: multicite-cut-may-strand-next-unit
cases.why: Task 1560: a cut ending right after a plural citation's first unit cannot know the citation ends there — another {key} unit may follow and would be stranded as prose.

cases.name: multicite-cut-takes-whole-citation
cases.why: Task 1560: a cut that covers every unit of the plural citation, with prose after it, takes the whole atom.

cases.name: linebroken-citep-drops-postnote
cases.why: Task 1560: TeX skips one line break between a command and its arguments (task 1510), so the [p.~3]{k} on the next line belongs to the atom and may not be dropped.

cases.name: commented-multicite-drops-second-unit
cases.why: Task 1560: a %-comment line end is argument gap too — the hand-written multi-line \cites keeps its second unit inside the atom.

cases.name: singular-citep-leaves-trailing-bracket
cases.why: Task 1560: a SINGULAR citation stops after its one unit, so prose `[sic]` after it is not the atom's and may be rewritten.
